findings.title: SQL Injection in Product Search
findings.description: The source code in `routes/search.ts` directly interpolates the `q` query parameter into a raw SQL string without sanitization or parameterization. An attacker can inject malicious SQL commands (e.g., `1' OR 1=1--`) to bypass filters, extract sensitive data from other tables, or potentially execute arbitrary commands depending on database privileges.
reproduction_steps: Unauthenticated access to the search endpoint
findings.impact: Full database compromise, data exfiltration, or denial of service
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries or an ORM method that automatically escapes inputs. For example, use `models.Product.findAll({ where: { name: { [Op.like]: `%${q}%` } } })` or bind parameters in raw queries.

observations.reason: Automated reproduction proof generator not registered for this claim type.

verifier_result.explanation: Requires manual verification or specialized test scenario.

findings.title: Insecure CORS Configuration
findings.description: The server responds to preflight requests with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, allowing any origin to make cross-origin requests. If the API relies on cookies or other implicit credentials for authentication (or if sensitive data is exposed without strict origin checks), malicious sites can read responses or make authenticated requests on behalf of users.
reproduction_steps: User visits a malicious website while authenticated to the target application
findings.impact: Cross-site request forgery (CSRF) or data exfiltration via cross-origin requests
findings.remediation: Restrict `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` to trusted domains only. Avoid using `*` if credentials are involved. Implement strict origin validation.

observations.limitation: Active probe skipped: active testing disabled or budget depleted.

verifier_result.explanation: CORS reflection probe requires active test authorization.

findings.title: Sensitive JWT Stored in localStorage
findings.description: The application stores the JWT authentication token in `localStorage`. Since `localStorage` is accessible via JavaScript, any Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability can allow an attacker to steal the token and impersonate the user.
reproduction_steps: Successful XSS attack or access to the browser's local storage
findings.remediation: Store tokens in `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, and `SameSite` cookies to prevent JavaScript access. Alternatively, use short-lived tokens with refresh mechanisms.

observations.reason: Automated reproduction proof generator not registered for this claim type.

verifier_result.explanation: Requires manual verification or specialized test scenario.

findings.title: Missing Content Security Policy (CSP)
findings.description: The absence of a Content Security Policy header allows the browser to execute inline scripts and load resources from untrusted origins. This increases the risk of successful XSS attacks and data injection.

evidence.explanation: Deterministic verification confirmed missing content-security-policy header.

findings.impact: Increased likelihood of XSS exploitation and data theft
findings.remediation: Implement a strict CSP header that restricts script sources to trusted origins and disallows inline scripts where possible.

verifier_result.explanation: Deterministic verification confirmed missing content-security-policy header.

findings.title: SQL Injection in Product Search
findings.description: An attacker supplies specially crafted input containing SQL syntax (e.g., apple%27)%20OR%201=1--) via the 'q' parameter, which is directly interpolated into the Sequelize raw query without parameterization, allowing manipulation of the query logic.
findings.impact: Unauthorized access to database contents, data exfiltration, modification, or deletion.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries or ORM query methods instead of string concatenation/template literals inside raw SQL queries.

findings.title: Sensitive Token Stored in HTML5 localStorage
findings.description: The application stores sensitive JSON Web Tokens (JWT) in localStorage, making them accessible to any JavaScript running on the same origin, thereby exposing them to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks.
reproduction_steps: Successful user authentication; presence of an XSS vulnerability on the site.
findings.impact: Token theft leading to session hijacking and account takeover.
findings.remediation: Store sensitive tokens in HTTP-only, Secure cookies rather than HTML5 localStorage.

findings.title: Overly Permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)
findings.description: The server responds with 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' allowing any arbitrary domain to make cross-origin requests to protected resources.
findings.impact: Exposure of sensitive API responses to unauthorized third-party websites.
findings.remediation: Restrict the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header to trusted origins rather than using a wildcard.

observations.limitation: Active probe skipped: active testing disabled or budget depleted.

findings.title: Missing Content Security Policy (CSP) Header
findings.description: The web application fails to return a Content Security Policy response header, increasing the window of opportunity for Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks.

evidence.explanation: Deterministic verification confirmed missing content-security-policy header.

findings.impact: Increased susceptibility to XSS attacks and unauthorized script execution.
findings.remediation: Implement a robust Content Security Policy (CSP) header specifying allowed sources for scripts, styles, and other resources.

verifier_result.explanation: Deterministic verification confirmed missing content-security-policy header.
